nary_nodes.label: Toddler food ultraprocessed research
evidence: Four out of five foods sold for toddlers in the United States are ultraprocessed, according to research that analyzed more than 2,700 products on grocery store shelves.

nary_nodes.label: Presentation of findings at ASN annual meeting
evidence: “We found toddler products which failed to meet WHO standards on sugar were four times as likely to be ultraprocessed,” said Hudson, who presented the preliminary research findings on Sunday at the annual meeting of the American Society for Nutrition.

nary_nodes.label: FDA proposed front-of-package labeling rule (2025)
evidence: The US Food and Drug Administration proposed a rule in 2025 for a mandatory, front-of-package labeling system for most packaged foods that would rate a food as “low,” “medium” or “high” in added sugars, sodium and saturated fat.

nary_nodes.label: Prior baby food additive study (January)
evidence: Prior research published in January found over 70% of 651 baby and toddler foods contained additives that emerging research has linked to inflammation and disruptions in the gut microbiome.

nary_nodes.label: Photographing toddler foods at grocery stores
evidence: To do the research, Hudson and her team photographed foods marketed to children between 6 and 36 months at 21 grocery stores in Austin, Texas.

nary_nodes.label: Nutrition label analysis of 2,783 products
evidence: Researchers analyzed nutrition labels on 2,783 products for grams of sugar, salt, saturated and unsaturated fat, total calories and additives.

nary_nodes.label: WHO Nutrient and Promotion Profile Model
evidence: Commercial foods marketed for children between 6 and 36 months should have no added sugar, artificial sweeteners or concentrated fruit juices, and limited saturated fats and sodium, according to the WHO Nutrient and Promotion Profile Model.

nary_nodes.label: Four out of five toddler foods are ultraprocessed
evidence: Four out of five foods sold for toddlers in the United States are ultraprocessed, according to research that analyzed more than 2,700 products on grocery store shelves.

nary_nodes.label: Nearly half of toddler foods fail WHO nutrition standards
evidence: Nearly half of those items also failed to meet at least one nutritional benchmark for children set by the World Health Organization.

nary_nodes.label: Sugar-failing products four times as likely to be ultraprocessed
evidence: “We found toddler products which failed to meet WHO standards on sugar were four times as likely to be ultraprocessed,” said Hudson, who presented the preliminary research findings on Sunday at the annual meeting of the American Society for Nutrition.

nary_nodes.label: Almost a quarter of foods exceed sodium recommendations
evidence: “Almost a quarter of the foods were higher in sodium than is recommended, and some were high in fat and calorie dense,” she added.

nary_nodes.label: High sugar/sodium foods also high in fat and calories
evidence: “Almost a quarter of the foods were higher in sodium than is recommended, and some were high in fat and calorie dense,” she added.

nary_nodes.label: Parents cannot identify ultraprocessed foods visually
evidence: “Many of them are high in sugar, high in sodium, but parents really cannot tell that from just walking down the aisle.”

nary_nodes.label: Ultraprocessed foods crowd out healthier options
evidence: “The problem isn’t just what’s in these high-sugar, high-salt ultraprocessed foods, it’s what they crowd out,” said Jane Houlihan, research director for Healthy Babies Bright Futures...

nary_nodes.label: Early taste preferences set for life
evidence: Early childhood is also the time when taste preferences are set for life, experts say.

nary_nodes.label: Industry misleads about healthiness of toddler foods
evidence: “Industry has marketed these toddler foods to make parents believe these foods were created for the health of toddlers, and it’s just not true.”

nary_nodes.label: Lack of universal definition for ultraprocessed foods
evidence: There is currently no universally accepted scientific definition of the term ‘ultraprocessed’ food, a spokesperson said.

nary_nodes.label: Additives linked to inflammation and gut microbiome disruption
evidence: Prior research published in January found over 70% of 651 baby and toddler foods contained additives that emerging research has linked to inflammation and disruptions in the gut microbiome.

nary_nodes.label: 71% of baby foods have additives as top ingredient
evidence: “What shocked me was the top ingredient in 71% of these baby foods wasn’t a fruit or vegetable — it was one or more additives,” Elizabeth Dunford told CNN previously.

nary_nodes.label: Parents advised to read labels and avoid added sugar, saturated fat, additives
evidence: “Look for ‘added sugar’ and ‘saturated’ fats on the nutrition label and if you see those, ‘put the food back on the shelf,’ Hudson said.

nary_nodes.label: Fruit juice concentrate indicates hidden added sugars
evidence: “Fruit juice concentrates are essentially only the sugar and flavor of fruit — everything else with nutritive value has been stripped away, almost like a simple syrup,” Hudson said.

nary_nodes.label: Parents encouraged to prepare foods at home
evidence: “As often as possible, parents should prepare healthy foods at home instead of using store-bought foods,” Houlihan said.

nary_nodes.label: Foods marketed to children under 4 exempt from FDA labeling rule
evidence: At this time, however, foods marketed to children under 4 would be exempt from that requirement.

nary_nodes.label: Consumer Brands Association says brands offer safe, affordable choices
evidence: The Consumer Brands Association, which represents industry, told CNN in an email that “America’s trusted household brands offer parents and caregivers a wide variety of safe, affordable and convenient product choices to meet different dietary needs, preferences and family budgets.”

nary_nodes.label: First 1,000 days vital for brain development
evidence: The first 1,000 days of a child’s life are vital for the growth and development of their brain and subsequent health, according to the American Academy of Pediatrics.

nary_nodes.label: Early ultraprocessed exposure may shape later preferences
evidence: Eating too many overly sweet, highly processed foods in childhood may lead to choosing sugar and artificial flavors over natural, nutrient-dense foods in the years to come.
